ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-contrast distribution characterized by dominant high-intensity (white) lateral lobes (~65%) and a central low-intensity (black) axial region (~35%) mapping to the peduncle area.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Two large contiguous high-intensity white regions occupy the lateral lobes. A central low-intensity black wedge-shaped blob originates from the insertion point and terminates at the median notch. High-frequency black/white pixel mottling occurs along the internal boundaries of the central black region and sporadically along the trailing edges.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped depression with a calculated interior angle of approximately 55 degrees and a significant depth-to-width ratio relative to the fluke center.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous, irregular high-frequency serration across the entire trailing edge. Notable higher-amplitude 'peaks' (jagged protrusions) are localized toward the distal tips of both lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Pronounced concave sweep along the trailing margin, curving upward and outward to form narrow, tapered lobe apices.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Distinct high-contrast white pixel clusters (rosette formations) localized at the extreme lateral tips of both lobes. Two isolated small, circular high-intensity spots are detected on the mid-right lobe surface.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several sub-vertical low-intensity linear streaks (marks) are visible within the high-intensity white region of the inner left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Localized barnacle colonization at the lobe tips. Irregular minor indentations along the trailing edge suggest mechanical wear or prior trauma.
other_distinctive_markers: Asymmetric dark pigmentation 'drip' patterns extending from the trailing margin into the white field of the left lobe.
